observations.message:
ETH transferred without address checks

Consider introducing checks for `msg.sender` to ensure the recipient of the money is as intended.

Low level call in Vault.withdraw(uint256) (src/Vault.sol#29-40):
	- (sent,None) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}() (src/Vault.sol#34)

Reentrancy in Vault.withdraw(uint256) (src/Vault.sol#29-40):
	External calls:
	- (sent,None) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}() (src/Vault.sol#34)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- balanceOf[msg.sender] = available - amount (src/Vault.sol#37)
	Vault.balanceOf (src/Vault.sol#9) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- Vault.balanceOf (src/Vault.sol#9)
	- Vault.deposit() (src/Vault.sol#21-26)
	- Vault.withdraw(uint256) (src/Vault.sol#29-40)

Reentrancy in Vault.withdraw(uint256) (src/Vault.sol#29-40):
	External calls:
	- (sent,None) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}() (src/Vault.sol#34)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- totalDeposits -= amount (src/Vault.sol#38)

Reentrancy in Vault.withdraw(uint256) (src/Vault.sol#29-40):
	External calls:
	- (sent,None) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}() (src/Vault.sol#34)
	Event emitted after the call(s):
	- Withdrawn(msg.sender,amount) (src/Vault.sol#39)

Reentrancy: State change after external call

Changing state after an external call can lead to re-entrancy attacks.Use the checks-effects-interactions pattern to avoid this issue.

Hint: State is changed at: `balanceOf[msg.sender] = available - amount`, `totalDeposits -= amount`
